periods.analysis: We start this run in yellow, not because the basics are loose, but because the road network is carrying more peak-hour load than it should. Fleet Uptime % is green at 94.3%, safely over the >=92 target, and the shop kept the front-line plow-dump and signal trucks available despite late-summer HVAC and brake work. Average Pothole Repair Time is also green at 3.1 days against the <=5 target, with Crew 2 holding the airport loop and Seaport Connector routes to a clean cadence. The watch item is Peak-Hour Travel Time Index at 1.32, above the <=1.3 target; two hundredths looks small on paper, but the pavement does not care about decimals when buses and freight are stacked at Gate 7.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green work green: continue the 10-day preventive-maintenance cycle for units F-214 through F-231 and keep hot-mix patch stock staged at North Yard before the first cold rain. For congestion, retime the Harbor Boulevard, Terminal Way, and 6th Avenue signal group in the evening peak and verify with Bluetooth travel-time runs, not just model output. I want a two-week watch log on Seaport Connector queues by direction, because that is where a 1.32 can become normal if we let it.

periods.analysis: The objective stays yellow, and the quarter-over-quarter direction confirms the pressure point. Fleet Uptime % slipped from 94.3% to 93.4%, down 0.9 percentage points, but remains green above the >=92 target after the shop absorbed winterization work on sweepers and dump bodies. Average Pothole Repair Time moved from 3.1 days to 3.9 days, up 0.8 days, still green versus the <=5 target as rain opened up older utility cuts on Bay Street and North Mercer. Peak-Hour Travel Time Index worsened from 1.32 to 1.4, still yellow and further from the <=1.3 target, driven by holiday cargo surges, airport arrivals, and the detour around Bridge Joint BJ-18.
periods.recommendations: Hold the fleet line by extending night-shift preventive maintenance through January for high-use units F-088, F-119, and F-203, and track parts delays separately from wrench time. Keep the pothole response under 5 days by pre-assigning one patch truck to the Bay Street/North Mercer grid after every 0.5-inch rain event. On travel time, implement temporary peak-hour turn restrictions at Terminal Way/Harbor Boulevard and ask Traffic Engineering to bring back before-and-after counts within 30 days.

periods.analysis: We are still yellow, but this quarter tells a mixed and useful story. Fleet Uptime % improved from 93.4% to 94.8%, up 1.4 percentage points, which says the winter maintenance discipline worked and the bay schedule was not just paperwork. Average Pothole Repair Time worsened from 3.9 days to 4.2 days, up 0.3 days, still green against the <=5 target but close enough that freeze-thaw work on Route 14 and the hospital hill cannot drift. Peak-Hour Travel Time Index held flat at 1.4 quarter over quarter, yellow and materially above the <=1.3 target, so we stabilized the congestion problem but did not solve it.
periods.recommendations: Sustain fleet uptime by locking in the weekly defect-review board for refuse packers and traffic-signal bucket trucks, with failures coded by asset ID and not buried in comments. Pull pothole repair back toward 3-day performance by assigning a second patch crew to Route 14, hospital hill, and the Mill Creek approaches for the next six weeks. For TTI, move from temporary fixes to an operations package: adaptive timing at 12 intersections on Harbor Boulevard and a freight-window agreement with the port for the 7:00-8:30 a.m. peak.

periods.analysis: Yellow remains the right rating, but Q2 shows the first real movement in the right direction on the weak leg. Fleet Uptime % rose from 94.8% to 96.2%, up 1.4 percentage points, well above the >=92 target after Fleet finished the spring PM blitz and retired two unreliable light-duty units. Average Pothole Repair Time improved from 4.2 days to 3.8 days, down 0.4 days, green against the <=5 target as warmer mix and tighter crew routing helped. Peak-Hour Travel Time Index improved from 1.4 to 1.33, down 0.07, but it is still yellow above the <=1.3 target; better is not done.
periods.recommendations: Keep the fleet gain by extending the PM blitz model to airport-rescue support vehicles and documenting downtime avoidance in hours so the budget request has evidence. Maintain pothole performance by using the PavementPro map to batch repairs by block face, not complaint order, especially in the Westport and South Bay districts. For travel time, keep the Harbor Boulevard adaptive timing live, add transit-signal priority checks on routes 3 and 18, and set 1.31 as the internal July watch threshold before we claim success.

periods.analysis: The score is still yellow, and the quarter-over-quarter numbers say our maintenance operation is strong while corridor demand keeps pushing back. Fleet Uptime % eased from 96.2% to 94.9%, down 1.3 percentage points, but remains green above the >=92 target; summer heat took its usual toll on refuse hydraulics and patrol SUVs. Average Pothole Repair Time improved sharply from 3.8 days to 3.0 days, down 0.8 days, green against the <=5 target after Crew 4 ran the Seaside Avenue and Eastgate resurfacing punch lists clean. Peak-Hour Travel Time Index stayed flat at 1.33, still yellow and still above the <=1.3 target, which means the Q2 gains held but did not compound.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 3.0-day pothole result by keeping one rapid-response patch truck in the Eastgate yard through the end of construction season and protecting that crew from non-emergency pulls. For fleet, pre-order hydraulic hoses, alternators, and cooling assemblies for the top 25 high-hour assets before the fall rain hits. On TTI, extend the signal timing package from Harbor Boulevard to the airport frontage roads and run police-assisted intersection clearing only where queue data show spillback, not where the phone rings loudest.

periods.analysis: Q4 stays yellow, and the congestion line moved the wrong way again. Fleet Uptime % dipped from 94.9% to 94.6%, down 0.3 percentage points, still green over the >=92 target and steady enough for storm response. Average Pothole Repair Time worsened from 3.0 days to 3.8 days, up 0.8 days, but remains green against the <=5 target as early storms reopened patches on older concrete panels near the waterfront. Peak-Hour Travel Time Index rose from 1.33 to 1.39, up 0.06, yellow above the <=1.3 target, with cruise-terminal events, airport holiday traffic, and lane closures at Culvert C-42 all showing up in the logs.
periods.recommendations: Keep fleet uptime above target by carrying the storm-season standby mechanic schedule on Fridays through February and assigning one lube truck to field service for drainage and street assets. Protect pothole response by staging cold mix at South Yard and requiring same-day triage on waterfront panel failures before they become axle-breakers. For TTI, freeze non-emergency lane closures on the Seaport Connector during the 4:00-6:00 p.m. peak and require Traffic, Port Operations, and Airport Ground Transportation to review weekly queue maps until the index is back below 1.35.

periods.analysis: We remain yellow, with dependable assets and road repair offset by a stubborn peak-hour network. Fleet Uptime % improved from 94.6% to 95.6%, up 1.0 percentage point, green against the >=92 target after the standby mechanic plan reduced tow-ins during the January storms. Average Pothole Repair Time worsened from 3.8 days to 4.4 days, up 0.6 days, still green versus the <=5 target but close enough to make me uncomfortable on the older arterials. Peak-Hour Travel Time Index was flat at 1.39 quarter over quarter, yellow and still above the <=1.3 target, so the closure controls stopped further damage but did not recover the corridor.
periods.recommendations: Sustain fleet performance by making storm standby a formal seasonal operating procedure and tying mechanic coverage to forecast rainfall and call volume. Pull pothole repair back below 4 days by adding a temporary two-person saw-cut and plate crew for failed utility trenches on Madison, Bay, and Airport Drive. For TTI, accelerate the Seaport Connector incident-response protocol, including tow rotation T-6 and camera verification at Gate 7, because a flat 1.39 is still a delay we are making residents and freight carriers pay for.

periods.analysis: The objective is still yellow, but Q2 shows measured recovery from the winter peak. Fleet Uptime % moved from 95.6% to 95.1%, down 0.5 percentage points, still green and comfortably above the >=92 target as we shifted from storm response to construction-season support. Average Pothole Repair Time improved from 4.4 days to 3.6 days, down 0.8 days, green against the <=5 target after the saw-cut crew cleared the Madison, Bay, and Airport Drive backlog. Peak-Hour Travel Time Index improved from 1.39 to 1.35, down 0.04, but remains yellow above the <=1.3 target; the network is better, not yet where it needs to be.
periods.recommendations: Keep fleet uptime resilient by extending condition-based maintenance to sweepers, signal trucks, and heavy patch units using the new telematics fault-code feed. Sustain the pothole gain by converting the temporary saw-cut crew into a summer backlog crew through September, with weekly production targets by street segment. For TTI, finish the airport-frontage signal retiming, add port gate appointment compliance reporting, and set a hard Q3 operating target of 1.32 or lower before we consider the yellow risk retired.

periods.analysis: Fleet uptime remains above target at an illustrative 94.4%, and pothole repair time remains within target at 4.1 days. Both slipped from June. The travel time index rose from 1.35 to 1.38 and remains above its 1.3 target, so the streets-and-fleet objective stays on caution.
periods.recommendations: Protect fleet maintenance capacity, keep the coordinated street-repair approach, and verify Harbor-Airport signal and closure effects before declaring congestion improved.
